grade.primary_choice: Keep Reverb: measure, tune, scale out, load-test at 2x, with a managed Pusher-compatible service as fallback
unsupported_claims: The 'tens of KB per connection' figure for a simple Go server is a loose generalisation presented without evidence
The 50 KB-per-connection Reverb figure is clearly hypothetical, but it is used to call the hosting-cost difference 'small' before any measurement
grade.notes: This is a strong, well-sequenced plan that rejects the Go rewrite before the deadline for the right reasons: deadline risk, bus factor and an unmeasured bottleneck. It covers ext-uv vs stream_select, one process per core, OS/proxy limits, a Redis pub/sub instance of its own, failure-mode load tests, reconnect jitter, managed fallback pricing and per-customer isolation; it only lightly covers N+1 capacity, graceful draining, load-balancer idle timeouts and explicit node-count cost estimates.
